title: Possibly erroneus "Fatal: repository contains errors" from check
body:
Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
`restic 0.18.0 compiled with go1.24.1 on linux/amd64`


What backend/service did you use to store the repository?
---------------------------------------------------------
Rclone (rclone v1.69.3), Jottacloud backend


Problem description / Steps to reproduce
----------------------------------------

I have switched cloud storage providers, moving repository data with rclone.

I don't know if the following is an artefact of the initial transfer, problems with the repository as such, or a bug in Restic.

What I note is that:

1. The Rclone part give occasional errors, prompting retries, after which Restic reports `check successful on second attempt` and the "original error", which seems to indicate that all is well after all, but
2. In the end, Restic reports `The repository is damaged and must be repaired. Please follow the troubleshooting guide at https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/077_troubleshooting.html .`

It's the mismatch between `check successful on second attempt` in part 1. and `The repository is damaged and must be repaired. Please follow the troubleshooting guide at https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/077_troubleshooting.html .` that confuses me.

It is possible that part 2. stems from an actual error with the data, but as far as I read the output, the only errors reported are the "original errors" from the attempt where Rclone errored out, but I don't feel confident stating whether the final error message is correct or not.

Command:
```
restic -r rclone:jottacloud:///<redacted> -o rclone.args='serve restic --stdio --retries 10 --transfers 8' check --read-data -verbose --password-file <redacted>
```

```
Fatal: repository contains errors
```

Expected behavior
-----------------

`restic check` reports `Fatal: repository contains errors` only if the checks that give errors during the run don't succeed on subsequent attempts.

To further limit confusion, there could be variants over the following:

1. No errors yield the appropriate message as usual
2. Errors that succeeded on subsequent yield a message along the lines of "errors were seen during the run, but they succeed on subsequent attempts, so the repository data is sound"
3. If errors occur, and one or more of them don't succeed on subsequent attempts, yield an error message that only specify the ones that didn't eventually succeed

Actual behavior
---------------

`Fatal: repository contains errors` is reported, but is not obvious to me whether this refers to errors that eventually succeed, or if one or more did not succeed at all.

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------

One of the following, the correct one being unknown to me:

1. Errors were reported during the run, one or more of which did not eventually succeed
1.1. In this case, the final error message is correct, but output is confusing
2. Errors were reported during the run, all of which eventually succeed, but a flag in the code that errors occurred wasn't cleared
2.1. In this case, the final error message is wrong, and the output is still confusing

Did restic help you today? Did it make you happy in any way?
------------------------------------------------------------
It usually does, and whereas what prompted me to write this is confusing, a resolution to it will make me fully happy again, as opposed to "only happy with all the other stuff that I usually am happy about :-)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: According to your log `data/8faca86749` does not appear to exist, at the very least. This correctly results in a fatal error that the repository is damaged. I am not sure in what way the output is confusing. There's a lot of error entries because of the repeated failures in downloading and verifying the data. It seems salient to include these entries as they're relevant to observe the health of the connection and the repository.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
It does indeed!

What seems unclear to me, is whether the reported check errors succeed in subsequent attempts, or whether they never did, and a handy place to do so would be in the summary at he end of the run.

E.g.:

1. `restic check` run starts
2. Rclone part fails and reports error
3. Restic part fails as a result, and reports error
4. Rclone and restic parts are retried, and either succeeds and report success, or are retried, but never succeed
5. `restic check` run ends
6. <wanted part, see below>

Part 6. above would be either a message at the that errors reported above can be ignored, since they succeeded eventually, or that some errors above can be ignored, since they succeeded eventually, but *some* of them failed, and a list of those.

As it stands now, I there is no indication at the end as to which parts of the errors above, if any, were eventually solved, and, hence, I am unsure as to whether to trust the ultimate conclusion of `Fatal: repository contains errors`

comments.body:
The `The repository is damaged and must be repaired.` error message is currently in place for `check successful on second attempt, original error` errors as those usually indicate a problem either with the host running restic or the backend. Either can compromise the integrity of the backup or prevent successful restores.

If we take a closer look at the `check successful on second attempt, original error [...]` errors,  there are only ciphertext errors but no complaints about a failed download or mismatching pack file hash. This means that the cause of the ciphertext errors is on the host running restic and not caused by the backend! Please run prime95 & memtest or similar to check that your system is actually stable.

Erring on the side of caution is, of course, laudable in general, but when the situation clears up, I, personally, don't think that one should decline acknowledging that clearing up actually did occur, and still insist on, unambiguously, reporting damage.

As always, though, there might be things that I have gotten wrong.

comments.body:
So, the `check successful on second attempt` errors in your case are definitely a bug in the retry handling. More precisely `check` didn't reset the errors found during the incomplete download attempt. This will be fixed by https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5495 .

But what worries me a bit is that there must be a second hidden problem underneath. Apparently restic received corrupted data from rclone in those failed downloads. An incomplete download wouldn't cause those `ciphertext verification failed` errors. Similarly, the returned data also couldn't have been only zero bytes as then the error would be `nonce is invalid`.

Thank you so much for looking into this, @participant2!

For a number of very obvious reasons, you know the code far, far, better than I do, so my understanding might be both naïve and wrong, but my mental image of what happens is that `rclone` begins to feed the data to `restic`, which, in turn, begins to process it and, naturally, when the `rclone` part errors out, `restic`'s processing fails, for obvious reasons<sup>1</sup>.

This, of course, shouldn't really be a problem, as we can, and do, retry up to a certain, configurable, number of times.

What your PR above seems to address, is that, previously, any error message emitted in the process, would later be flagged as evidence of corruption, even though the corruption was actually in transit, and was remedied by a subsequent retry.

Now, as you mention, there seems to be a hard-coded limit of exactly one retry at a certain point in the code, and I am certain that it is there for a good reason, that my very limited understanding of the code does not allow me to comment competently on, but I will note that at some point, I actually, with `rclone`, downloaded the entirety of the repo data to local storage, and local repo copy verified without errors with the plain "file" backend (although errors did occur in the download process, which were cleared up by retrying).

That last point seems to suggest, at least to me, that `rclone` and `restic` might have evolved to have slightly differing ideas of how to interchange the data, and that this is the point of corruption, as opposed to the repo itself being corrupt.

An obvious next step, of course, is for me to either build `restic` myself with the PR pulled in, or wait for the next release, and then simply give it a try at verification again?

<sup>1</sup> I read the second part of https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5467#issuecomment-3263855126 to mean that my understanding above is either actually, or ideally, wrong, and that no data should be received by `restic` from `rclone` (or at least not processed), until the download is complete, but could it be, as I allude to above, that while this assumption might very well have been correct at the outset, this might not actually be the case at present - again in light of the fact that a complete repo download (with `rclone`) yields a local storage repo that `restic` actually *does* proclaim to be free from corruption?

comments.body:
> 1 I read the second part of [#5467 (comment)](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5467#issuecomment-3263855126) to mean that my understanding above is either actually, or ideally, wrong, and that no data should be received by `restic` from `rclone` (or at least not processed), until the download is complete, but could it be, as I allude to above, that while this assumption might very well have been correct at the outset, this might not actually be the case at present - again in light of the fact that a complete repo download (with `rclone`) yields a local storage repo that `restic` actually _does_ proclaim to be free from corruption?

rclone already sends data to restic while rclone is still downloading it. If the download is interrupted, then restic just receives too little data and retries the download. However, in your case something else has seemed to happen: the download from jottacloud was both too short and included corrupted data. The latter shouldn't happen normally. My PR ensures that errors from a too short + corrupted download are completely ignored if the download retry is successful+valid. 

If `check` detects a corrupt file, it rechecks it a second time. This has been added to better detect failed verifications due to hardware issues. Note that the second check by prune is independent of the general retry mechanism for backend operations. 

That is the `Load(<data/0b641d3c7b>, 34691933, 0) operation successful after 1 retries` messages above are standard behavior by restic and nothing to worry about (well, at least as long as there aren't too many retries). The `check successful on second attempt, original error pack` code path wasn't used at all in this case.

> I wonder if this can be taken to mean that when that failure is reported without the patch, then we can conclude that it being reported was an erroneous consequence of the lack of retry handling that the patch remedies?

Well actually the error reporting didn't play well with the retry handling. Now, that error is now just silently swallowed as the retry did work.
